title: Colour change — switching yarn mid-work
subtitle: Complete the stitch before the change with the new colour on the last pull-through
excerpt: Colour changes in crochet happen on the last yarn-over pull-through of the stitch before the change, not at the start of the new stitch. Drawing through the final loops with the new yarn is what creates a clean colour transition. The old yarn is dropped and carried, or cut and rejoined, depending on the distance to the next use.

glossaryTerms.definition: Switching from one yarn colour to another during crochet. The change is made on the last pull-through of the last stitch in the old colour — draw the final loops through with the new yarn. The old colour is then carried (float) or cut and woven in.

heroPrompt: A small crochet swatch in two colours — navy and cream DK yarn — showing a clean horizontal colour change between rows, close-up showing the change row.

inlineDiagramTopics.description: The last dc in old colour with 2 loops on hook, new colour yarn-over about to draw through both loops

content.text: happens inside the last stitch of the old colour, not at the start of the new one. This counterintuitive timing is what makes the transition clean — the new colour is already on the hook when the first full stitch of the new section appears, so no colour bleeds forward from the old shade.
Work to the last dc in the old colour. Insert hook, yarn over with old colour, draw up a loop — 2 loops on hook.
Drop the old yarn. Yarn over with the new colour. Draw through both loops on the hook.
The new colour is now on the hook. Continue with the new colour for the turning chain and the rest of the row.

attrs.title: Carrying vs cutting
attrs.body: If the old colour returns within 3-4 stitches, carry it by working over the unused strand — the carried strand is enclosed inside the new stitches and hidden. If the old colour won't be needed for 5+ stitches or doesn't return at all, cut it and leave a 10 cm tail to weave in.

items.symptom: A fleck of the old colour shows at the start of the new section
items.cause: Changing colour on the first stitch of the new row rather than the last stitch of the old row
items.fix: Make the colour change one stitch earlier — change on the final draw-through of the last stitch before the colour section ends.

content.text: Tapestry crochet carries two colours simultaneously in every stitch, working over the non-active colour to create colourwork patterns within a single row. Surface slip stitch applies colour lines to a finished piece without reworking the base fabric.
